# Overview

`bottom-UpR` provides a generic interface for Bayesian bottom-up population
modelling using INLA-SPDE. COUNT responses can be modelled with Poisson or
negative-binomial likelihoods, while PPB responses can be modelled with Gamma
or lognormal likelihoods.

# Flexible hierarchy

Hierarchical effects are optional:

```r
effects <- list(
  list(column = "source", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "settlement", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "region_settlement", model = "iid", prediction = "known"),
  list(column = "ea_id", model = "iid", prediction = "known")
)

fit <- bottom_up(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = c("roads", "water", "market"),
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects
)
```

Any of these effects can be removed. Other grouping effects can be substituted
without changing the package internals.

# Validation with fold-specific selection

```r
cv100 <- bottom_up_cv(
  data = ea,
  response = "ppb",
  buildings = "buildings",
  response_type = "ppb",
  likelihood = "gamma",
  covariates = candidate_covariates,
  coords = c("x_m", "y_m"),
  hierarchical_effects = effects,
  method = "spatial_block",
  folds = 5,
  block_size = 100000,
  covariate_selector = bottom_up_inla_selector,
  selector_args = list(fallback = 8),
  prediction_draws = 300
)

cv100$metrics
cv100$metrics_by_fold
cv100$selected_covariates
plot_cv_diagnostics(cv100)
```

Scaling and the selector are both estimated inside each training fold.

# Observation-level posterior results

```r
obs <- observation_predictions(fit, draws = 500)
head(obs)

plot_observed_fitted(fit)
plot_bottom_up_residuals(fit)
plot_posterior_fixed(fit)
plot_posterior_hyperparameters(fit)
plot_hierarchical_effects(fit, effect = "source")
plot_spatial_field(fit)
```

# Fine-grid joint-posterior prediction

The same posterior sample IDs are retained across every prediction chunk:

```r
grid100m$national <- "Cameroon"

pred <- predict_bottom_up(
  fit,
  newdata = grid100m,
  population = TRUE,
  draws = 1000,
  chunk_size = 50000,
  return_draws = FALSE,
  aggregate_by = c("national", "region", "division"),
  omit_effects = c("source", "ea_id")
)

head(pred$summary)
pred$aggregates$national
pred$aggregates$region
pred$aggregates$division
```

For PPB models, building exposure is applied by multiplying PPB by mapped
buildings. For count models, buildings are already included as an offset and are
not multiplied again. Cells without mapped buildings are structural zeros.
